idiom_name: trait-object component slots (Vec<Box<dyn Component>>) or an ECS crate (hecs, bevy_ecs)
implementation_notes: Rust has no inheritance and no invisible shared identity, so the container is written explicitly: a Component trait for the hook, a struct owning Vec<Box<dyn Component>>, and an update loop that calls through the trait object - dynamic dispatch needs a pointer because trait objects are unsized (doc.rust-lang.org). When the capability set is fixed, an enum of component variants is the idiomatic alternative: allocation-free, exhaustively matched, and free of dyn. For data-oriented storage delegate to an ECS crate (hecs keeps a minimalist World with queries; bevy_ecs stores components per type and schedules systems), which is the usual answer once per-box layout becomes the bottleneck.
pitfalls: Each Box<dyn Component> is its own allocation plus a vtable call; if profiling shows layout is the bottleneck, move to an ECS crate rather than adding more boxes.
The borrow checker forbids passing &mut self to a component while iterating the component list - split the entity's fields (destructuring borrows) or pass the shared state separately.
Box<dyn Component> erases the concrete type, so recovering a component by type needs the Any/downcast_ref dance; prefer named fields or an enum when a system needs one specific component.

variants.name: ECS crate world (hecs / bevy_ecs) with per-type storage and queries
variants.implementation_notes: In hecs the entity stays a lightweight id: components are plain structs stored per type and behaviour is ordinary code iterating a query (write free systems or use bevy_ecs's scheduler for parallel execution and change detection). Choose it when entity counts or iteration cost dominate; the price is that component access is a query rather than a field access, and structural changes are explicit world operations.
pitfalls: Component types are the storage key: two components of the same type on one entity are impossible, so model 'two of the same' as an id or a collection inside the component.
Queries borrow the world, so a system that needs another entity's components must go through the world API again instead of holding a second query.
bevy_ecs systems run in a schedule: reading a component changed this frame requires change detection, not a flag you maintain yourself.
